finding.claim: The user identity comes straight from a client-supplied HTTP header (X-Session-User-Verified). No session, signature or token is checked. Any caller can impersonate any user by setting the header to that user's name, which bypasses every ACL check.
finding.source: The attacker-controlled request header `X-Session-User-Verified`. The attacker only needs to know or guess a grantee's user ID.
finding.sink: The protected operations: `del STORE[fid]` in delete_file (views.py:18) and `f["name"] = ...` in rename_file (views.py:27).

trace.note: before_request sets g.user = request.headers.get("X-Session-User-Verified"), unauthenticated and unvalidated
is_allowed only checks that action is in resource['grants'][user], so the spoofed name matches the real owner's grants
rename_file uses the same g.user for the 'write' check, so the attacker can rename any file

finding.guards_checked: I found no authentication middleware, no signature or session verification, and no code that strips the header. The ACL logic itself is sound, but it trusts the identity it is given. The header name implies a trusted upstream proxy sets it. Nothing in this repo enforces that the proxy strips or overwrites client-sent copies, so the finding depends on that deployment assumption. Only views.py and acl.py are in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none in repo; ACL checks at acl.py:5/9-10 are correctly enforced (ensure_allowed aborts at views.py:17, is_allowed tested at views.py:25) but only validate the header-supplied identity
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (views.py:11 takes g.user straight from the header, and the sinks at views.py:18 and :27 are gated only by acl.py:5 against that value), but whether a trusted proxy strips or overwrites client-sent X-Session-User-Verified is a deployment fact that isn't visible in this repo (only views.py and acl.py), so exploitability can't be decided from the code.

verdict_facts.guard_found: Trusted upstream middleware populates request identity (per project facts); the "-Verified" header is its output. Downstream ACL checks are effective: ensure_allowed aborts 403 (acl.py:9-10) and is_allowed's result is tested (views.py:25).
verdict_facts.reason: views.py:11 reads the identity header, but the project facts state identity is set by trusted upstream middleware outside this directory. The finding admits it depends on an unproven assumption that the proxy doesn't strip client-sent copies, so it isn't a flaw in this module. The ACL checks at views.py:17 and views.py:25 block users without grants (acl.py:5-10).
